Fit a RuleFit Model

Source: R/rule_ensemble.R
rule_ensemble.Rd

rule_ensemble() fits a RuleFit model with the boosting library chosen by method. It passes its arguments to rule_ensemble_xgb(), rule_ensemble_lgb(), or rule_ensemble_ctb().

Usage

rule_ensemble(
  x,
  ...,
  method = c("xgboost", "lightgbm", "catboost"),
  trees = 50,
  mtry = 1,
  learn_rate = 0.01,
  tree_depth = 4,
  min_n = 5,
  penalty = 0.001,
  mixture = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

Depending on the context:

  • A data frame of predictors.

  • A matrix of predictors.

  • A formula specifying the outcome terms on the left-hand side, and the predictor terms on the right-hand side.

  • A recipe specifying a set of preprocessing steps created from recipes::recipe().

...

Other arguments passed to the function chosen by method:

  • The outcome y (for a data frame or matrix x), or data (for a formula or recipe x).

  • weights, for case weights (not used with a recipe; see the "Case weights" section).

  • Named options for the boosting model and the glmnet model; see the "Boosting and glmnet options" section.

method

A single character string for the boosting library: "xgboost" (the default) uses rule_ensemble_xgb(), "lightgbm" uses rule_ensemble_lgb(), and "catboost" uses rule_ensemble_ctb().

trees

An integer for the number of trees contained in the ensemble.

mtry

The proportion of predictors randomly sampled, on (0, 1]. For xgboost and lightgbm, the predictors are sampled at each split. For catboost, they are sampled for each tree level (catboost's rsm).

learn_rate

A number for the rate at which the boosting algorithm adapts from iteration-to-iteration (specific engines only). This is sometimes referred to as the shrinkage parameter.

tree_depth

An integer for the maximum depth of the tree (i.e. number of splits) (specific engines only).

min_n

The minimum number of data points in a node needed to split it further (min_child_weight in xgboost and min_data_in_leaf in lightgbm). catboost does not use min_n; see Details.

penalty

A non-negative number representing the total amount of regularization (specific engines only).

mixture

A number between zero and one (inclusive) denoting the proportion of L1 regularization (i.e. lasso) in the model.

  • mixture = 1 specifies a pure lasso model,

  • mixture = 0 specifies a ridge regression model, and

  • 0 < mixture < 1 specifies an elastic net model, interpolating lasso and ridge.

Available for specific engines only.

verbose

A single logical. If TRUE, the boosting library prints its training log, and rule_ensemble_ctb() warns when min_n is given and ignored.

Value

A rule_ensemble_xgb, rule_ensemble_lgb, or rule_ensemble_ctb object, depending on method. Each inherits from "rule_ensemble"; see rule_ensemble-object for their elements.

Details

The main arguments (trees, mtry, etc.) are translated to each library's own parameters.

catboost and min_n

catboost does not use min_n. Its default "SymmetricTree" grow policy has no minimum node size. When method = "catboost", the default value of min_n is ignored silently. A value that is given is also ignored, with a warning when verbose = TRUE. To set a minimum node size for catboost, pass min_data_in_leaf along with grow_policy = "Depthwise" or grow_policy = "Lossguide".

Case weights

Case weights are used to fit both the boosted trees that create the rules and the glmnet model that is fit to the rules. Rows with a weight of zero are not used to decide which rules are removed for having a single unique value or being linear combinations of other columns.

For the data frame, matrix, and formula methods, pass the weights to weights. A case weights column cannot also be a predictor. For the recipe method, add the weights as a column of data that is created by hardhat::importance_weights() or hardhat::frequency_weights(); recipes::recipe() gives these columns the "case_weights" role, so they are not used as predictors.

Boosting and glmnet options

Named options for the boosting model and the glmnet model are given together as one set in .... Each option is sent to one of the two models by its name:

  • Options for the boosting library go to the boosting model. The valid names depend on the library; see the ... argument of rule_ensemble_xgb(), rule_ensemble_lgb(), or rule_ensemble_ctb().

  • Arguments of glmnet::glmnet() go to the glmnet model (e.g., standardize or penalty.factor). path_values, a numeric vector of penalty values for the glmnet path, also goes to the glmnet model; see parsnip::glmnet-details for how it is used.

A name that is valid for both models goes to the boosting model. An unknown name is an error. Options that rbe sets itself are also errors; use the main arguments (e.g., trees or learn_rate) instead.

References

Friedman, J, and B Popescu. 2008. "Predictive Learning via Rule Ensembles." The Annals of Applied Statistics 2 (3): 916-54.

Chen, T, and G Guestrin. 2016. "XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System." In Proceedings of the 22nd ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, 785-94.

Ke, G, Q Meng, T Finley, T Wang, W Chen, W Ma, Q Ye, and TY Liu. 2017. "LightGBM: A Highly Efficient Gradient Boosting Decision Tree." In Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, edited by I Guyon, U Von Luxburg, S Bengio, H Wallach, R Fergus, S Vishwanathan, and R Garnett. Vol. 30. Curran Associates, Inc.

Prokhorenkova, L, G Gusev, A Vorobev, AV Dorogush, and A Gulin. 2018. "CatBoost: Unbiased Boosting with Categorical Features." In Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, edited by S Bengio, H Wallach, H Larochelle, K Grauman, N Cesa-Bianchi, and R Garnett. Vol. 31.

See also

rule_ensemble_xgb(), rule_ensemble_lgb(), rule_ensemble_ctb()

Examples

if (rlang::is_installed("xgboost")) {
  set.seed(1)
  fit <- rule_ensemble(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars, trees = 5, penalty = 0.1)
  fit

  predict(fit, mtcars[1:3, -1])
}
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   .pred
#>   <dbl>
#> 1  20.5
#> 2  20.2
#> 3  23.5
